title: Sifted colimits and separately colimit-preserving bifunctors
statement: Use universes, simplicial sets, quasicategories, spaces, coherent diagrams, products, weak contractibility and colimits as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the simplex category $\Delta$ as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Write $\mathcal S$ for the infinity-category of small spaces. A small infinity-category $K$ is called sifted when its colimit functor $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)\to\mathcal S$ on small spaces preserves finite products, including the empty product. Every such $K$ is weakly contractible. If $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ are infinity-categories admitting $K$-indexed colimits and $F:\mathcal C\times\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ preserves them separately in each variable, then $F$ preserves $K$-indexed colimits as a functor on the product: for diagrams $P:K\to\mathcal C$ and $Q:K\to\mathcal D$, the canonical cocone to $F(\operatorname{colim}P,\operatorname{colim}Q)$ is colimiting. The nerve $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted in this space-valued sense.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Definition 5.5.8.1, Lemma 5.5.8.4, Propositions 5.5.8.6-5.5.8.7, Lemma 5.5.8.11 and Remark 5.5.8.12. Space-colimit characterization: Kerodon Tag 0704, Proposition 9.7.2.12, https://kerodon.net/tag/0704, with its proof in the following variant; read online. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Use the space-valued definition of siftedness in the statement, including preservation of the empty product. The first paragraph of [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus] applies to an arbitrary small infinity-category, not only a nerve: it identifies this condition with nonemptiness and finality of the diagonal $\delta:K\to K\times K$, and asserts weak contractibility. Thus $K$ is weakly contractible, and restriction along $\delta$ takes any existing colimit cocone on $K\times K$ to a colimit cocone on $K$. Only this finality assertion, not an ordinary-category finality statement, is used below.

source.place: Definition 5.5.8.1, Proposition 5.5.8.7, and the space-valued characterization of Lemma 5.5.8.11 / Remark 5.5.8.12; characterization reused from the existing sifted-index node.

proof.text: Choose colimit cocones $p:P\to\Delta_Kc$ and $q:Q\to\Delta_Kd$, where $c=\operatorname{colim}_KP$ and $d=\operatorname{colim}_KQ$; as coherent transformations they are simplicial maps $p:K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$ and $q:K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal D$ restricting to $P$, $Q$ over the vertex $0$ and to the constant diagrams at $c$, $d$ over the vertex $1$. Put $H(i,j)=F(P(i),Q(j))$, $U(i)=F(P(i),d)$ and $Z=F(c,d)$. Let $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\sigma_2):\Delta^2\to\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ be the $2$-simplex with vertices $(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)$, and define $\Theta:K\times K\times\Delta^2\to\mathcal E$ by $\Theta(i,j,s)=F\bigl(p(i,\sigma_1(s)),q(j,\sigma_2(s))\bigr)$; it is a simplicial map because simplicial products are formed degree by degree, so it is a $2$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(K\times K,\mathcal E)$. Its face opposite the last vertex is $(i,j,t)\mapsto F(P(i),q(j,t))$, a transformation $H\to U\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$; for fixed $i$ it is the image of $q$ under $F(P(i),-)$, the row cocone $H(i,-)\to\Delta_KU(i)$, colimiting by preservation in the second variable. Its face opposite the first vertex is $(i,j,t)\mapsto F(p(i,t),d)$, the pullback along $\mathrm{pr}_1$ of the image $U\to\Delta_KZ$ of $p$ under $F(-,d)$, colimiting by preservation in the first variable. Its remaining face is the cocone $\gamma:H\to\Delta_{K\times K}Z$, $\gamma(i,j,t)=F(p(i,t),q(j,t))$, whose leg at $(i,j)$ is exactly $F(p_i,q_j)$. Thus $\Theta$ exhibits $\gamma$ as the composite of the row cocones with the outer cocone, without any choice of horn filler; all higher coherences come from applying the simplicial map $F$ to the coherent cocones $p$ and $q$. All shapes used are small. This constructs the candidate product-indexed cocone $\gamma$ without assuming that $\mathcal E$ has all $K\times K$-colimits.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.8.6, construction of the two-variable cocone from separate preservation.

proof.text: Apply the dual clause of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $T=\Delta_K:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$, with the full subcategory all of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$. Existence of $K$-colimits in $\mathcal E$ and the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] supply its universal-arrow hypothesis for every diagram. We obtain a coherent $L:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)\to\mathcal E$, a universal cocone $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to\Delta_K L$, and the dual coherent-diagram mapping-space formula, compatible with evaluation. This is only a $K$-colimit construction; no $K\times K$-colimit is assumed.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.5.8.6, successive-colimit argument: assembly of row colimits, using the existing dual parametric universal-arrow theorem.

proof.text: Degreewise exponential adjunction for simplicial sets identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(K\times K,\mathcal E)$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E))$; let $\widetilde H$ be the curried $H$. Under this identity the row face of $\Theta$ from step 2 is a coherent transformation $\alpha:\widetilde H\to\Delta_K\circ U$. Its vertex cocones are colimiting by separate preservation, as checked there. Apply [lem-coef-coherent-row-colimit-comparison] with $I=J=K$, $R=\widetilde H$ and the $L,\eta$ just obtained. It gives a coherent equivalence $a:L\widetilde H\to U$ whose composite with the universal row cocone is homotopic, as a coherent transformation, to the specified row face $\alpha$. Thus the comparison includes all coherence data, not merely equivalences of row apices.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.5.8.6 / Lemma 5.5.2.3, comparison of the coherent row colimits; the comparison is now a separate lemma.

proof.text:
For every $z\in\mathcal E$, the outer cocone criterion, the row equivalence $a$, the dual coherent-diagram formula of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows], and currying give, in order,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(Z,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(U,\Delta_Kz)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(L\widetilde H,\Delta_Kz)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E))}(\widetilde H,\Delta_K(\Delta_Kz))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K\times K,\mathcal E)}(H,\Delta_{K\times K}z).$$
The formula sends a transformation to its composite with $\eta\widetilde H$. The compatibility homotopy in the preceding step therefore identifies this composite of maps with precomposition by the row cocone followed by the outer cocone. The explicit $2$-simplex $\Theta$ from step 2 identifies that composite with $\gamma$. Thus precomposition by $\gamma$ is an equivalence for every $z$. The dual criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves that this very cocone is colimiting. This supplies the needed $K\times K$-colimit using only $K$-colimits.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.5.8.6 and the absolute successive-colimit argument of Lemma 5.5.2.3, mapping-space test for the explicit composite cocone.

proof.text: Apply the diagonal-finality assertion of [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus] to the product-indexed colimit cocone just proved. Its restriction is a colimit cocone on $i\mapsto F(P(i),Q(i))$ with vertex $F(c,d)$, and its leg is $F(p_i,q_i)$, by the leg calculation in step 2. This is exactly the canonical cocone specified in the item. To interpret this as preservation on the product category, observe that a cocone in $\mathcal C\times\mathcal D$ is a pair of cocones and its mapping-space test is the product of the two tests, since simplicial products and right-pinched mapping spaces are computed coordinatewise. The two tests are equivalences because $p$ and $q$ are colimiting; their product has the product of their inverses as inverse. The dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore makes $(p,q)$ a colimit cocone with vertex $(c,d)$. The image under $F$ is the cocone just proved colimiting.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.8.6, restriction of the product-indexed cocone along the final diagonal.

proof.text: The final clause of [lem-coef-sifted-nerve-index-calculus] states that $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted with precisely the space-valued definition used here. This proves the remaining assertion. In particular its use in steps 1-4 concerns homotopy-coherent simplicial diagrams, with all their higher compatibility data, and makes no identification with ordinary set-valued siftedness.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.8.4; space-valued formulation via Lemma 5.5.8.11 and Remark 5.5.8.12.

proof_origin.place: Agent reconstruction of Proposition 5.5.8.6, expanding the successive-colimit argument of Lemma 5.5.2.3 with existing parametric universal arrows; the existing sifted-index node supplies the criterion, weak contractibility, and Lemma 5.5.8.4. HTT read online, not archived in literature/.
